title: Generic-point unit for a normal constant sheaf
statement: Let Y be an integral scheme whose local rings are integrally closed, let g be the canonical morphism from the generic point of Y, and let M be a module over a commutative ring Λ. The unit from the constant Λ-module sheaf on Y to its pushforward along g is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Choose an affine open chart Spec R containing the image of a geometric point s. Its stalks are isomorphic to stalks of Y, so R is an integrally closed domain by the normal-stalk criterion. The adopted chart maximal-ideal theorem supplies a local full strict-henselization ring C and a chart ring map whose spectrum followed by the chart immersion equals strictLocalizationToBase s. Apply the adopted affine-chart ind-etale theorem with the identity spectrum isomorphism to equip C with an ind-etale R-algebra structure. Work throughout with this full presentation.

source.place: Tag 03Q9, degree zero and canonical restriction construction; Tag 09Z5

proof.text: Present C as a filtered colimit of etale R-algebras. The etale-colimit normal-local-domain theorem gives IsDomain C and injectivity R→C. Tensoring C with the fraction field of R is localization of C at the images of nonzero elements of R; injectivity ensures these images are nonzero, so this localization is a domain.

source.place: Tag 03Q9, degree zero and canonical restriction construction; Tag 09Z5

proof.text: The spectrum of that tensor-product domain is the pullback of the generic point of Spec R and Spec C. Remove the common open-immersion factor in the two pullback legs, then use the open-immersion stalk isomorphism at the generic point to identify this pullback with the strict fibre over the generic point of Y. Thus this fibre is integral and therefore connected.

source.place: Tag 03Q9, degree zero and canonical restriction construction; Tag 09Z5

proof.text: The adopted full-model constant-strict-fibre comparison identifies the unit on each geometric stalk with the canonical coefficient map to sections on the connected strict fibre. The latter is invertible: transfer the abelian-group constant-section theorem through ModuleCat to AddCommGrpCat, using preserved sheafification and reflection of isomorphisms. The coefficient germ to the constant-sheaf stalk is invertible by the generic Point.toPresheafFiber_presheafFiberConstIso_hom and Point.isIso_presheafFiber_map_toSheafify_const API, combined with Point.toPresheafFiber_naturality. Cancel the coefficient germ and strict-fibre comparison to prove the stalk unit invertible. No small/full fibre transport is needed.

source.place: Tag 03Q9, degree zero and canonical restriction construction; Tag 09Z5

proof.text: Transport stalk invertibility through the canonical universe-lifting isomorphism of fibre functors. Apply the conservative family of geometric stalks to obtain IsIso for the original unit, with its statement unchanged.
